chapter: Paris 1951-70 and return to New York
title: Black writers in Paris, Sartre and Pigalle versus the Left Bank
summary: Asked about Cesaire, Damas and Senghor, Butler says the Left Bank students were separate from his Pigalle world, though he met Sartre and actors at Club d'Or.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, did you meet -- oh, for the hair?
When you were over there, whether in the 30's or the 50's/ did you meet any of the writers, like Aime Cesaire, Leon Damas, Leopold Senghor?
I mean some of the black writers? There were some guvs from Martinique, like Cesaire was from Martinique.

No, this was an African boy, "I spit on your tomb." I met him, because see, basically they were going to school there. And they were in Vellon Colombe (PHONETIC), in that section. See, because each person had a section. See, there was the Colombe, I'm Pigalle. I'm a Pigalle man. And this other part, the Left Bank (inaudible). Then you had --

That was over the Saint Germain, we called it, sector. That was by the cathedral of Notre Dame. Those people, they were students, so I didn't meet too many of them. I was down meeting the Clush(?) D'Or people down there. I was meeting real people down there, all the actors and everything. (Unintelligible) Nicolas (PHONETIC) and all those big actors, because they hung out there.
